issue.title: Fix ACE memory-review notification nested Textual app crash
issue.description: While implementing plan:202608/pager_screen.md, the same nested Textual app failure class was found in the memory-review notification action. `handle_memory_review` suspends ACE and calls `MemoryReviewTuiApp(...).run()` from the running ACE app. That still enters Textual synchronous App.run behavior inside an already-running event loop. This is out of scope for the pager-screen change but should be fixed by hosting the review UI as a screen or otherwise avoiding nested App.run from ACE.

task_type_fields.impact: Opening a memory-review notification can crash or tear down the ACE control surface instead of returning to the Agents/Patches tabs. It is the same nested Textual App failure class as the pager `v` keypath that plan:202608/pager_screen.md fixed.
task_type_fields.repro: Open an ACE notification whose action is `memory_review` while the ACE TUI is already running. `handle_memory_review` enters `app.suspend()` and calls `MemoryReviewTuiApp(initial_proposal_id=...).run()`, which drives Textual through its synchronous `App.run` path from inside ACE active event loop. Existing coverage in `tests/ace/tui/test_memory_review_notification_action.py` stubs the review app `run()` method, so it does not execute the failing nested Textual path.
